editorial:
You probably remember the headline: a plane lands on the Hudson River and everyone survives. But this movie shows you what happened after the cameras stopped rolling. Tom Hanks plays Captain Sully, a pilot who suddenly has to defend his split-second decision to land on water instead of trying to reach a runway. The story jumps between the crash itself and the tense investigation that follows, keeping you on edge the whole time. It feels grounded and real, never flashy, and you really feel the weight of what Sully went through.

The acting is top-notch, especially Hanks, who makes you feel every bit of stress and doubt. The pacing is tight, and the crash scenes are gripping without being over the top. The only downside is that some investigation scenes drag a little. If you enjoy true stories about ordinary people doing extraordinary things, this one is for you. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Sully and his co-pilot face a hearing where investigators claim they could have made it back to a runway. Sully asks them to run the simulations again, this time adding the human delay of reacting to the emergency. When they do, both simulations crash. The investigators admit Sully made the right call. The movie ends with Sully and his co-pilot walking through New York, greeted by cheering crowds, finally at peace with what happened.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true stories about everyday heroes.
